trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,2). So the line goes left.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (left from number 3) was wrong, so the line must go up.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Going left would leave both number 5 and cell (3,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Going right would strand number 5: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (6,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going left would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going up would leave number 10 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Cell (4,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Cell (2,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
